transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’ve been more wound up at home. I’m still holding it together at work, but I’ve been short with people at home and it’s been harder to keep up with my coursework. I’ve also stopped doing things like fishing, woodworking, and the first-aid workshops that usually help me clear my head.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in most things you usually enjoy?
I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in most things, no. I just haven’t been making the time or having the energy to do some of the things I usually enjoy.
Do you feel this tension and irritability are mainly because your father-in-law moved in with you?

Yes, I think that’s the main trigger. Since he moved in, I’ve been more on edge at home—shorter with people, and I’m falling behind with coursework. I’m still doing my job okay, but I’ve stopped making time for fishing and woodworking and those first-aid workshops that usually help me clear my head.
Is this situation at home causing you significant distress?

Yeah, it is. I’m managing at work, but once I’m home I feel more wound up and short-tempered than usual, and the coursework is slipping. I’ve even stopped making time for fishing, woodworking, and the first-aid workshops that normally help me clear my head.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed. I’ve mostly noticed being tense and irritable, especially at home.
Outside of the situation with your father-in-law, have you been worrying a lot about other things too?
Not really. It’s mostly the situation at home that’s been getting to me.
Did these problems start after your father-in-law moved in?
Yeah. He moved in about four months ago, and within the first month or two, once we were figuring out the routines and caregiving, I started feeling the strain.
Has this situation at home been affecting your ability to function in daily life?
I’m still able to do my EMT work, but I’ve fallen behind on my paramedic coursework. And I haven’t been showing up regularly for the community first-aid workshops I usually help with.
Have you been feeling sad most days?
I’m not sure I’d say sad most days. It’s more that I’ve been feeling strained by everything at home.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively even when you’re not dealing with the situation at home?
I haven’t really noticed that. Most of my worry seems tied to what’s going on at home.
Has the tension at home been causing problems in your relationship with your spouse or other family members?
Yeah. I’ve been more wound up and short with my spouse since my father-in-law moved in. I’m trying to keep it together, but at home it comes out more than I’d like.
Have you been feeling down or hopeless nearly every day?
I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down or hopeless nearly every day. It’s more the stress at home getting to me.
Do your reactions to your father-in-law moving in feel stronger than you would normally expect for this kind of situation?

Yeah, I think so. I’m managing at work, but at home—and even with my coursework—I’m a lot more wound up and short-tempered than I usually am. I’ve also stopped doing things like fishing and woodworking that normally help me clear my head.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?
No, I don’t think it’s been like that most of the day, every day.
Are these problems still happening now?
Yes. There hasn’t really been a break from it—my father-in-law is still living with us, and we’re still trying to adjust to the caregiving arrangement.
Do you feel anxious even when nothing related to your father-in-law or home situation is going on?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it in situations that have nothing to do with home.
Do you feel nervous or anxious most days?
I’m not sure I’d say most days. It seems to come up more when I’m dealing with things at home.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
I haven’t really noticed any change in my appetite.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any particular trouble sleeping.
Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty?
No, I haven’t really been feeling worthless or especially guilty.
